english.title: Burglary dwelling - attempt grievous bodily harm
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having entered as a trespasser

(A)_[a dwelling,]_
(B)_[part of a dwelling,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ADDRESS..), attempted to inflict grievous bodily harm upon **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..) a person therein
english.legislation: Contrary to section 9(1)(b) of the Theft Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
entered as a trespasser
a dwelling / part of a dwelling
attempted to inflict grievous bodily harm

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 28(c) of Schedule 1 to the Magistrates Courts Act 1980 provides that if in the course of a dwelling house burglary any person is subjected to violence or threats of violence, then that offence CANNOT be tried summarily, therefore this offence is triable only on indictment.
(ii) IMPORTANT - Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Two prior convictions for domestic burglary may make him/her liable to a minimum sentence of three years imprisonment under the provisions of section 314 of the Sentencing Act 2020.
(iii) See also offence wordings: H1646, H2043 and H2051.
